A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same k-LLMmeans research, despite the revised title and organization. Text, equations, tables, and figures support comparison throughout. v1 has no appendices; v2 includes readable Appendices A–D.

before.justification: v1 reports original static and streaming clustering experiments in Tables 1–2 and an original sequential-clustering case study in Section 7.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds conventional-baseline and multiple-LLM results, including extended results in Appendix B.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same periodic summary-based centroid updates, document sampling, cluster assignments, and weighted mini-batch updates. The four experimental variants are renamed from 1/5/FS1/FS5 to single/multiple/FS-single/FS-multiple without changing their stated procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Bank77, CLINC, GoEmo, MASSIVE domain and intent clustering, the same 2020–2023 StackExchange subsets, and the 2021 AI-site case study. v2 relocates dataset descriptions to Appendix A; additional models and comparisons do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds GMM, agglomerative clustering, and spectral clustering to the static comparisons previously limited to k-means and k-medoids. Table 3 also compares against ClusterLLM, IDAS, and LLMEdgeRefine using results explicitly attributed to Feng et al.; these are reported comparisons, not established reruns. Streaming comparator membership is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a controlled FS-multiple/e5-large comparison across five LLM backbones and comparative LLM-call accounting. Retained experiments preserve the stated dataset sizes, chronological batching, iteration budget, and sampling sizes. Accuracy was already described as measured in v1, so its newly printed scores do not establish a newly introduced metric.

E4.justification: v1 varies embeddings, summary frequency, and prompt sample size while using GPT-4o exclusively. v2 adds systematic sensitivity analysis across GPT-3.5, GPT-4o, Llama-3.3, DeepSeek-V3, and Claude-3.7, covering all benchmark tasks in Table 10. New Figure 1 also illustrates escape from a k-means local minimum. The original streaming case study is retained.

E5.justification: v1 reports averages over ten static seeds and five streaming seeds without dispersion estimates. v2 Appendix B adds standard deviations for static, multiple-LLM, and streaming results. The stated run counts remain unchanged. Section 5.1 calls these standard errors, inconsistently with the appendix descriptions and captions.

E6.justification: v2 adds accuracy scores, new baseline and LLM-backbone results, and LLM-call counts. All original static NMI/dist entries survive in Appendix B within rounding, and streaming NMI means are unchanged; streaming centroid-distance results are omitted. Some newly reported baseline values disagree internally: CLINC GMM accuracy with text-embedding-3-small is 78.9 in Table 1 but 80.484 in Table 6.

T1.justification: v2 removes v1's explicit unit-norm embedding assumption and associated Euclidean/cosine equivalence statement. It also states an O(kl) LLM-call bound. The objective and centroid equations remain substantively unchanged, and neither version supplies a theorem or proof establishing the asserted convergence guarantees.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions broaden the empirical claim from outperforming k-means to outperforming other traditional baselines and achieving results comparable to state-of-the-art LLM clustering with fewer calls. v2 also explicitly claims a provable descent property and convergence regardless of summarization quality, strengthening the earlier general preservation-of-properties claim.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations of backbone robustness, near-state-of-the-art cost-efficiency, and recovery from faulty summaries. It replaces v1's DistilBERT qualification with a universal smaller-distance interpretation, although Table 2 retains CLINC distances of 0.343 versus k-means' 0.340. The fixed-number-of-clusters limitation is removed, while Appendix D adds sensitive-domain deployment considerations.

D1.justification: New Appendix C discloses approximately one week of simulations on a standard laptop, API usage, roughly 120 million tokens and $700 in OpenAI costs, and under $30 for other LLMs. v1 provides no comparable resource accounting. Existing prompt examples, sampling parameters, and raw/clean dataset availability statements are retained.

R1.justification: The related-work base and positioning as a scalable, interpretable enhancement of k-means largely remain. v2 adds the Instructor reference and sharpens its criticism of competing pipelines' optimization landscapes and query requirements. Moving related work from Section 2 to Section 8 is organizational rather than a literature expansion.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract and substantial introductory and results passages, moves related work toward the end, separates static and streaming experiments, and relocates dataset descriptions into Appendix A. It also revises the title and variant terminology and combines the conclusion and limitations within a Discussion section.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout and substantially restructures the experimental tables into main-text summaries and detailed appendix displays. It adds the four-panel PCA illustration and new comparison and uncertainty tables. v1 Figures 1–2 are retained, resized, and renumbered as v2 Figures 2–3.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's narrower, means-only evaluation, v2 provides useful baseline comparisons, LLM sensitivity results, dispersion estimates, and resource accounting. However, new main-text and appendix baseline scores conflict, and stronger interpretations exceed the evidence: Table 2 contradicts uniformly smaller centroid distances, while Table 3 includes only a 1.8-fold call reduction against LLMEdgeRefine on CLINC despite claiming orders-of-magnitude savings. Stronger descent guarantees receive no proof. These problems affect the reliability of the expanded central claims, leaving the net quality direction unclear.
